description: Truvity's shared renovate baseline. Consumed as `github>truvity/ci-workflows`.
Lives here, and not in github-structure, for two reasons: this repo is what a
repository DOES (github-structure is what one IS, and is a generic product that
must stay free of estate-specific content), and it is PUBLIC — a preset in the
private repository would be unreadable by the public renovate app.
Repo-specific rules stay in each repo's renovate.json and layer on top; only
rules that are true estate-wide belong here.
postUpdateOptions.gomodTidy: `go get` alone bumps go.mod but leaves
go.sum carrying the OLD dependency's hashes. Any consumer whose
recipes run `go mod tidy` (the estate norm) then fails every job on
the bump PR with "modified the working tree" — tidy is not part of
`go get`, and renovate does not run it unless told to. Security pass,
The automergeable batch: everything non-major, in one PR.
minimumReleaseAge: a release must be three days old before it joins the batch.
Without it the batch is rebuilt on every run as upstream ships, and an
automation that only merges a PR whose checks were already green when its
run started can never catch it: access-roster#47 sat green for three days
while being rebuilt nightly (2026-09-16). Three days also lets a bad
release be yanked before it is ever proposed.

packageRules.description: Majors always get a human. The `major` label is load-bearing: the fleet renovate job's approval step refuses to approve anything carrying it.

description: BELOW 1.0 A MINOR IS A BREAKING CHANGE. Semver only promises
compatibility from 1.0 onward, but renovate classifies a 0.x minor as
non-major, which sweeps it into the automerged batch above.
Incident (2026-09-05, a private monorepo): @truvity/gateway-auth v0.5.2 ->
v0.7.1 rode in that way, carrying jose v5 -> v6 with it. The batch was
red for days and cost a full night to bisect. That repo already had this rule
for @openid4vc/**; it is a property of 0.x versioning, not of one
package, so it belongs to every repo.
The regex is `/^v?0\./`, not `/^0\./`: Go's module datasource carries
the `v` prefix on currentVersion (truvity/audit v0.2.5), so the bare
form never matched a single Go module and every 0.x Go minor rode the
automerged batch silently. Security pass, 2026-09-29.
devbox.json pins (C6 of the component contract: every package pinned,
never `latest`) are only real pins if something keeps them from going
stale. `devbox update` (the fleet parity job) only re-resolves whatever
a package is ALREADY declared as — a `latest` request gets the newest
nix build, but an exact pin like `gopls@0.23.0` stays exactly there
forever; parity never bumps a version number. Renovate's `devbox`
manager is the only thing that can move a pin forward, and it is
enabled by default (no `enabledManagers` restriction here narrows it
out) — explicit `matchManagers` below is belt-and-braces against a
future edit to the generic rules above scoping them down by manager.
Several repositories carry a per-repository `"ignorePaths":
["devbox.json", "devbox.lock"]` left over from when those files held
`latest` entries the devbox datasource had nothing useful to compare
against; now that C6 requires exact pins, that override has to be
removed from each such repository's own renovate.json or this rule
never sees the file — ignorePaths is local config, and a preset does
not get to override what an extending repository set explicitly.
The toolchain triad (go, golangci-lint, govulncheck) is OWNED by
devbox-update, not Renovate, under EITHER manager that can see it:
gomod (go.mod's `toolchain` directive — already excluded above,
kept here too so both live in one place) and now devbox (the same
three as devbox.json package keys, newly reachable now that the
devbox manager is enabled). golangci-lint and govulncheck each
embed the Go release they were built with and refuse a newer one,
so the three can only move together — devbox-parity pins them as
one unit (docs/devbox-update.md) and verifies they agree; a
Renovate PR bumping `go` alone here would silently reintroduce
exactly the mismatch that ownership was built to prevent.
Repository-level copies of the gomod half of this rule are
harmless duplicates and do not need to be removed.
Monorepos move as a unit. Five separate open PRs for @veramo/core,
core-types, did-comm, did-manager and did-resolver v7 (truvity/core,
2026-09) are individually unmergeable by construction — the packages
pin each other. One PR per monorepo is the only reviewable shape.
